title: Realtime Conversational Video with Pipecat and Tavus — Chad Bailey and Brian Johnson, Daily & Tavus
talk_summary: A Pipecat/Daily and Tavus talk about building realtime conversational video bots, covering model choice, an orchestration layer (frames/processors/pipelines), and deployment. It is mostly a framework/product pitch for voice-video agents, with a few transferable orchestration and observability ideas.

takeaways.what_they_do: They model every event (audio chunks, VAD signals, LLM tokens, context turns) as typed 'frames' passed through composable 'processors' arranged in a pipeline, so behavior is described declaratively and each stage is swappable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a processor just takes in some frames and outputs other frames

takeaways.what_they_do: Run a second pipeline concurrently (e.g., classify voicemail vs human, sentiment) that emits a signal to route the main pipeline down a branch.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Run one model to determine and then it sends a signal to the back to the pipeline to say do the voicemail branch or do the human branch.

takeaways.what_they_do: A context aggregator waits for a turn-complete signal, then groups accumulated transcript fragments into one context frame that triggers the LLM, rather than firing on every fragment.
takeaways.evidence_quote: group all of the various pieces of transcription we've gotten over the past few seconds together and emit a single context aggregation frame

takeaways.what_they_do: Ship a debug panel showing internal pipeline state and per-stage metrics so you can see why the bot behaved a certain way and where latency comes from.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can see some of like the interesting guts of what's happening inside Pipcat in that debug panel

takeaways.technique: Turn-detection / response-timing as separate small models
takeaways.what_they_do: Use dedicated small models for 'is the user done' and 'how fast to respond' rather than letting the main model decide, decoupling timing from generation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Our turn detection model is a multilingual model that determines when a person is done speaking.

takeaways.technique: REST API to spin up per-session bot instances
takeaways.what_they_do: A lightweight REST endpoint starts a fresh bot instance per user session and connects it to the transport, avoiding long-lived shared processes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you need something to relatively quickly spin up a new instance of your bot and connect it to that user
